# Josh Lake, joshlake.ai

> Serial entrepreneur thinking about AI and the convergence of energy and intelligence. Colorado, USA.

## About Josh Lake

Josh Lake is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, and builder. He is currently focused on AI and the convergence of energy and intelligence — what becomes possible when both get cheap and abundant. He is the founder of Electrify Everything Now (free home electrification calculators). He co-founded Elephant Energy, a home electrification platform, and served as its CTO for five years. Earlier in his career, he was Head of Operations at Nuro (autonomous delivery), COO of Evercar/Vision Fleet (shared EV fleets), and Sr. Program Manager at Amonix (concentrated solar, world-record CPV modules). He holds a B.S. in Materials Science & Engineering from MIT and a Mechanical Engineering certificate from Stanford.

## Expertise

- AI and the convergence of energy and intelligence
- Speed to power: large load interconnection, queue reform, time-to-energized for data centers
- Grid capacity and risk: interconnection risk, curtailment risk, flexible load, behind-the-meter generation
- AI data center infrastructure and energy demand growth
- AI-native services businesses: delivering professional-services scope with agent-run workflows
- Agents for operations: multi-agent systems, agentic operating systems for companies
- Home electrification: heat pumps, induction stoves, EV chargers, electrical panels, smart load management
- AI implementation in small and mid-size companies
- Climate technology and clean energy
- Autonomous vehicles and electric vehicle operations
- Startup operations, scaling, and go-to-market

### Invention > Automation
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/invention-over-automation
- Description: Eight observations from months of hands-on building with AI agents, organized around a causal chain: energy makes tokens, tokens make intelligence, intelligence unlocks invention, and invention unlocks abundance. Argues invention beats automation (referencing Mark Zuckerberg's August 2026 essay "The Future Is For Everyone"), that most new invention will be combinatorial (drugs and chemistry, movies, recipes and food, content, products, materials), and asks whether the invention loop itself can be automated. Predicts 1,000x more software that is single-user, perfectly customized, locally run, unreviewed, disposable and transient by design, with the same shift producing live 1:1 tutoring for any subject. Argues agents finally deliver real automation, that agents only need to do work economically valuable to someone, that you should start with one specific named problem (invoice review, commissioning docs, incentive and rebate forms, SOW creation, electrical design, technical escalation, recruiting screens) rather than a generic "customer service agent," and that marketplaces of task-specific agents wired together via LLMs, MCPs, and APIs resemble manufacturing engineering. Argues the "product overhang" from today's frontier models is enormous because context, memory, permissions, interface, and trust are what's missing rather than capability; that outcomes replace output, people pay for decisions, speed, and outcomes rather than hours or seats, and speed to innovate beats cost savings inside companies; that model routers and especially agent routers (routing on capability, task complexity, cost, quality and reliability, data privacy, security, scalability, repeatability, and general versus industry-specific models for HVAC, automotive, marketing, and legal) become a control-system layer; that well-trained skills for robots will be sold as products, starting with the dull, dangerous, and dirty; and "vibe-living," where you request a verifiable outcome and pay for it while software, robots, and capital are assembled on the fly and torn down when done, pushing toward idea-to-object. Names energy and electrification as the long-form bottlenecks to abundance, argues high price electricity is the biggest blocker and cheap electricity the only path forward (solar and storage, nuclear, geothermal, wind, SMRs, balcony solar), and notes the grid has more buffer than assumed. Closes on work: acknowledges real displacement in customer support and similar repeatable knowledge work, then argues that when intelligence goes to zero the bottleneck moves to selection, direction, taste, and deployment, trust becomes currency, human roles move upstream (deciding what should exist) and downstream (making it real, trusted, and adopted), and "labor as an experience" expands service quality (small classrooms, an hour with the best doctor). Frames the shift from an efficiency mindset to an abundance mindset and ends on the view that most people aren't ambitious enough and an abundant future needs to get built.

### A Neo-Electrification Company?
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/neo-electrification-company
- Description: Essay asking what a homeowner-centric, AI-enabled, national "neo-electrification" company would look like — one that combines heat pumps, solar and storage, electrical work, financing, incentives, field execution, and a home energy operating system. Maps the players circling the opportunity (heat pump installers like Elephant Energy, Jetson, Zero Homes, QuitCarbon, Quilt, and Forge; solar and storage platforms like Sunrun and Base Power; OEMs like Mitsubishi, Daikin, LG, and Carrier; utilities and CCAs; and smart-panel companies like SPAN). Argues AI's real value is reducing soft costs across design, incentives, marketing, commissioning, service, forecasting, working capital, and margin, and looks at European models (Aira, 1KOMMA5°, Thermondo, Enpal, Octopus). Concludes the winner will be semi-vertical, AI-enabled, nationally repeatable but locally excellent, utility-aware, and obsessed with project-level economics.

### Not All Tokens Are Equal
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/not-all-tokens-are-equal
- Description: Essay arguing that AI compute is not a single market. Maps the token economy into five workloads (capability creation, commodity batch, premium interactive, agentic outcome, local/autonomous), each with different economics, latency, geography, and power profile. Argues cheap energy and cheap intelligence are now the same race, and the next infrastructure winners will integrate compute, energy, networking, orchestration, capital, and physical deployment.

### This Is How I Would Implement AI at a 40-Person Startup
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/ai-at-a-startup
- Description: Practical playbook for implementing AI at a small (~40-person) company. Covers real leadership buy-in as prerequisite; the productivity-vs-transformation choice; standardizing on one LLM and one prototyping tool; distinguishing AI-empowered, AI-first, and AI-native; pragmatic guardrails and admitting policing is hard; solving for context before capability; crawl-walk-run maturity (agents, gems, and skills come last); treating agents like employees; restructuring roles, titles, and workflows; and building a shared culture of experimentation with leading indicators (adoption, happiness, token-maxing). Based on leading the AI rollout at Elephant Energy.

### The Electrification Sequencing Problem
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/electrification-sequencing
- Description: Decision framework for homeowners deciding what to electrify first. Covers appliance replacement timing, energy math by appliance type, panel capacity, solar sizing, and navigating the rebate landscape. Based on thousands of home electrification projects.

### You Probably Don't Need a Panel Upgrade
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/panel-upgrade-myth
- Description: Deep technical guide explaining why most homes do not need a $5,000-$10,000 electrical panel upgrade to electrify. Covers NEC Section 220.87 load studies, tandem breakers, load-sharing devices, dynamic load management, subpanels, and smart panels. Profiles 12 companies building panel-avoidance technology.
